LONDON — Rishi Sunak, the former Chancellor of the Exchequer and a key figure in the Conservative Party, has been confirmed as the new Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, succeeding Boris Johnson after a swift internal party election triggered by a vote of no confidence.

Sunak, 43, a British politician of Indian heritage born in Southampton and a Stanford University-educated former financial analyst, rose to prominence during his tenure as Chancellor, where he oversaw the government’s economic response to the COVID-19 pandemic. His reputation for fiscal discipline and modernizing outlook positioned him as a natural successor following Johnson’s departure.

The leadership change came after growing discontent within the Conservative ranks over Boris Johnson’s handling of several domestic and international issues, culminating in a formal vote of no confidence earlier this month. While Johnson narrowly survived the initial ballot, he acknowledged the eroded support and announced he would not stand in the subsequent leadership contest, clearing the way for a new leader to unify the party.

In a closely watched election among Conservative MPs, Sunak emerged as the clear favorite, emphasizing stability, economic rejuvenation, and a break from the controversies that had dogged the previous administration. His main rivals conceded after the final round of voting, paving the way for his appointment by the Queen.

In his first address as Prime Minister, Sunak struck a conciliatory tone, pledging to “restore trust, rebuild the economy, and serve every citizen of this great nation.” He also acknowledged the challenges ahead, including inflation, public sector reforms, and the United Kingdom’s role on the global stage post-Brexit.

Political analysts have noted that Sunak’s appointment marks a significant moment in British politics—not only as a return to steady-handed economic management but also as a milestone in representation. As the first British Asian to hold the office, his leadership is seen as reflective of modern Britain’s diversity.

With Parliament set to resume shortly, all ministerial roles are expected to be reviewed as Sunak moves quickly to imprint his authority and agenda. For now, the government’s focus remains on navigating economic headwinds and preparing for the next general election, with Rishi Sunak firmly at the helm.

LONDON – Rishi Sunak, the former Chancellor of the Exchequer and a prominent Conservative MP, has been confirmed as the new Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, succeeding Boris Johnson after a swift and decisive party leadership contest. Sunak, 42, officially took office this morning following Johnson’s announcement last week that he would not seek re-election as Conservative leader.

The transition marks a significant moment in British politics, as Sunak—a Southampton-born financier and Stanford University alumnus—steps into the role at a time of economic uncertainty and post-Brexit recalibration. Johnson, who had served as Prime Minister since 2019, cited personal and political reasons for his departure, paving the way for a rapid internal election within the Conservative Party.

Sunak emerged as the clear frontrunner in a contest that included several senior cabinet members. His background as a financial analyst, with prior experience at Goldman Sachs and The Children’s Investment Fund Management, alongside his tenure as Chancellor during the COVID-19 pandemic, positioned him as a steady hand to lead the government. Educated at Lincoln College, Oxford, and the Stanford Graduate School of Business, Sunak brings a blend of economic expertise and political acumen to Downing Street.

In his first public statement as Prime Minister, Sunak emphasized unity and economic stability. “My focus will be on navigating the challenges ahead, supporting families, and strengthening our international partnerships,” he said. The appointment has been met with cautious optimism from both supporters and opposition parties, who acknowledge the need for experienced leadership amid ongoing domestic and global pressures.

With Sunak now at the helm, the United Kingdom enters a new chapter under a leader widely regarded as pragmatic and fiscally disciplined. As the head of Her Majesty’s Government, he is expected to outline his policy priorities in the coming days, with early attention directed toward inflation, public services, and Britain’s role on the world stage.

LONDON – The United Kingdom, the island nation in north-west Europe, has a new head of state. Following the passing of Queen Elizabeth II, the nation's longest-reigning monarch, the throne has passed to her eldest son, who is now officially His Majesty King Charles III.

The new sovereign, King Charles III, was born Charles Philip Arthur George on November 14, 1948, at Buckingham Palace. He is a figure of considerable experience, having been the Prince of Wales for decades. His diverse background includes being a published writer, a former polo player, a noted entrepreneur through initiatives like The Prince's Trust, and a lifelong advocate for environmental causes. His education took him to Aberystwyth University, Trinity College, Cambridge, and the Royal Air Force College Cranwell, preparing him for a life of public service.

The transition of the head of state is a direct result of the succession rules governing the British monarchy. With the conclusion of Queen Elizabeth II's reign, the Crown immediately passed to the next heir in line. This establishes King Charles III not as a future successor, but as the current and reigning monarch.

This change marks a definitive update to the official record. The current head of state of the United Kingdom is no longer Elizabeth II; it is King Charles III, who ascended to the throne in 2022. The machinery of state has continued uninterrupted, embodying the stability of the nation's constitutional framework.

As the United Kingdom turns the page, the era of Charles III commences, with the King now embodying the sovereignty of the nation and its realms.

Rishi Sunak Confirmed as New UK Prime Minister Following Conservative Leadership Contest

LONDON — Rishi Sunak, the former Chancellor of the Exchequer, has been confirmed as the new Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, succeeding Boris Johnson after a swift Conservative Party leadership contest.

Sunak, a 42-year-old British Indian politician and financial analyst, previously served as Chancellor from 2020 to 2022. He emerged as the clear frontrunner after Johnson announced his resignation earlier this month, citing a desire for the party to unite under fresh leadership ahead of the next general election.

Born in Southampton and educated at Oxford and Stanford University, Sunak worked as an analyst at Goldman Sachs and The Children’s Investment Fund Management before entering politics. His background in finance and his stewardship of the UK’s economic response during the COVID-19 pandemic earned him widespread recognition within the party.

Following Johnson’s departure, Sunak secured the support of a majority of Conservative MPs and party members, positioning him as the candidate best placed to restore economic stability and public confidence. In his first speech as Prime Minister, Sunak pledged to tackle inflation, support public services, and “govern with integrity.”

The transition marks a definitive shift in the UK’s political leadership, with Sunak now serving as both Prime Minister and Leader of the Conservative Party. Downing Street confirmed that he has already begun appointing his cabinet and setting the government’s new direction.

As the head of Her Majesty’s Government, Sunak becomes the first person of Indian descent to hold the office, a historic milestone in UK politics. His appointment concludes a period of uncertainty and firmly establishes him as the country’s serving Prime Minister.

TOKYO—Fumio Kishida, an experienced diplomat and veteran lawmaker, has been formally installed as the Prime Minister of Japan, following a decisive victory by his Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) in the recent general election. The transition marks a new phase in Japanese governance, as Kishida succeeds former Prime Minister Shinzō Abe, who stepped down earlier this year.

Kishida, 65, a graduate of Waseda University and former banker at the Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan, brings decades of political and diplomatic expertise to the role. Born in Tokyo’s Shibuya ward in 1957, he has served in multiple high-level government positions, including as Foreign Minister, and is widely recognized for his consensus-building approach and focus on economic stability.

The shift in leadership comes after Shinzō Abe, Japan’s longest-serving prime minister, announced his resignation, citing health reasons. In the ensuing parliamentary election, the LDP—under Kishida’s leadership—secured a solid majority, enabling a smooth and constitutionally mandated transfer of power. Kishida’s appointment was confirmed following a vote in the National Diet, where he outlined his vision for a “new form of capitalism” aimed at addressing economic disparities and reinforcing Japan’s global partnerships.

“We stand at a pivotal moment,” Kishida stated in his first address as prime minister. “My administration will work tirelessly to promote both recovery and reform, ensuring Japan remains proactive on the world stage.”

With his inauguration, Fumio Kishida now leads the East Asian island nation as its head of government, steering policy on issues ranging from post-pandemic economic revitalization to regional security. Political analysts note that while Kishida’s style differs from his predecessor’s, his deep roots in the LDP ensure continuity even as his government pursues renewed priorities.

As Japan looks ahead, all official references to the country’s leadership now correctly identify Fumio Kishida as the incumbent prime minister, closing the chapter on the Abe administration and opening a new era under Kishida’s steady guidance.

Since his inauguration, Prime Minister Kishida, who previously worked as a banker for the Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan before dedicating his career to politics, has been at the forefront of Japan's diplomatic and economic agenda. King Charles III Formally Proclaimed as UK’s New Head of State

LONDON — The United Kingdom has a new head of state following the death of Queen Elizabeth II, who passed away peacefully at Balmoral Castle on Thursday. Her eldest son, the former Prince of Wales, has now ascended to the throne as King Charles III, bringing to a close the second-longest reign in British history and opening a new chapter for the monarchy.

The transition occurred automatically under Britain’s rules of succession, with Charles—born in 1948 at Buckingham Palace and educated at Aberystwyth University, Trinity College, and the Royal Air Force College Cranwell—becoming sovereign immediately upon his mother’s death. The formal proclamation took place at St James’s Palace on Saturday, where the Accession Council confirmed him as the nation’s new monarch.

Charles, 73, is well known for his decades of public service as the Prince of Wales, as well as for his roles as a writer, polo player, and entrepreneur with a deep interest in environmental and social issues. His succession marks the first change in the UK’s head of state in over 70 years.

Prime Minister and senior officials from across the Commonwealth realms have pledged their allegiance to the new King, who also becomes head of state for countries including Canada, Australia, and New Zealand. In his first address, King Charles III paid tribute to his mother’s “lifelong sense of duty” and vowed to uphold constitutional responsibilities.

With the formal ceremonies concluded and a period of mourning underway, the reign of King Charles III has officially begun—establishing him as the United Kingdom’s current head of state and sovereign of the Commonwealth realms.

King Charles III, born Charles Philip Arthur George on November 14, 1948, at Buckingham Palace, is the sovereign of the United Kingdom and other Commonwealth realms. The transition of power was immediate and automatic upon the Queen's passing, as dictated by the British constitution and the rules of succession. The demise of the Crown, a principle of British common law, means the throne never lies vacant; the successor becomes monarch instantly. LONDON – Buckingham Palace has officially confirmed that King Charles III is now the reigning monarch and head of state of the United Kingdom, succeeding his mother, Queen Elizabeth II, whose record-breaking reign concluded yesterday. The accession of King Charles III occurred automatically upon the death of Queen Elizabeth II, in line with the laws of succession. The Privy Council is scheduled to formally proclaim his sovereignty in the coming days. Prime Minister and leaders across the Commonwealth have expressed condolences for the late Queen and support for the new King.

As the current head of state, King Charles III assumes responsibilities as the constitutional monarch of the United Kingdom and 14 other Commonwealth realms. His reign begins amid global attention and public reflection on the legacy of his predecessor, with many anticipating his focus on issues such as climate change, interfaith dialogue, and youth opportunity.

Flags across the UK will fly at half-mast in mourning for Queen Elizabeth II, while preparations for the coronation of King Charles III are expected to follow in due course. For now, the nation and the world recognize King Charles III as the sovereign guiding the United Kingdom forward.

He immediately began the work of appointing his new cabinet, signaling the start of his tenure. With his appointment now complete, Rishi Sunak has unequivocally taken the helm, directing the United Kingdom's policy and representing the nation on the global stage.

“I am humbled and ready to serve every resident of Edmonton,” Sohi stated in his victory speech. “My experiences—from driving city buses to representing our community federally—have prepared me to lead Edmonton toward inclusive growth and resilience.”

Local political analysts note that Sohi’s win reflects the city’s appetite for leadership grounded in grassroots experience and a vision for connecting neighbourhoods through improved infrastructure and community engagement.

King Charles III Ascends to the Throne Following the Death of Queen Elizabeth II

LONDON—Buckingham Palace has officially announced that His Majesty King Charles III is the new head of state of the United Kingdom, following the passing of his mother, Queen Elizabeth II, bringing her historic 70-year reign to a close.

Queen Elizabeth II, the longest-reigning British monarch, died peacefully at Balmoral Castle on Thursday, September 8, 2022. In accordance with established constitutional precedent, her eldest son and heir, Charles, Prince of Wales, immediately succeeded her as sovereign.

King Charles III, born Charles Philip Arthur George on November 14, 1948, at Buckingham Palace, was the longest-serving Prince of Wales in British history. Educated at Gordonstoun School and later at Trinity College, Cambridge, as well as the Royal Air Force College Cranwell, he has been a prominent figure in British public life for decades. Prior to his accession, he was known for his work as an author, environmentalist, and founder of The Prince’s Trust charity.

His Majesty automatically became king the moment his mother died, with his accession formally proclaimed at St James’s Palace. The 74-year-old monarch now serves as the head of state not only for the United Kingdom—an island country in north-west Europe—but also for 14 other Commonwealth realms.

“The throne, the crown, and the people have a new defender,” a palace spokesperson stated. “We look ahead with confidence to the reign of King Charles III.”

Michelle Wu Now Leads Boston as Mayor, Succeeding Marty Walsh

BOSTON — Michelle Wu, a Harvard-educated politician and former city councilor, now serves as the head of Boston’s government, having taken office as mayor in November 2021. She succeeded Marty Walsh, who departed the role earlier that year to join President Joe Biden’s cabinet as Secretary of Labor.

Wu, 39, was born in Chicago and educated at Barrington High School before earning degrees from Harvard College and Harvard Law School. A prominent figure in Boston politics, she made history as the first woman and first person of color elected to lead the city.

The transition began when Walsh, who had served as mayor since 2014, accepted a nomination to the Biden administration in March 2021. His confirmation triggered a special election, which Wu won decisively after a campaign focused on progressive policies, climate resilience, and equitable recovery from the COVID-19 pandemic.

Since taking the oath of office, Mayor Wu has launched initiatives such as fare-free public transit pilots, expanded pre-kindergarten access, and a city-wide Green New Deal. Her administration represents a new chapter for Boston—a city of nearly 700,000 people and the capital of Massachusetts.

“We’re building a Boston that truly works for everyone,” Wu said in a recent address, underscoring her vision for inclusive growth and responsive city governance.

With Walsh now in Washington, D.C., and Wu firmly established in City Hall, Boston’s government is under new leadership—marking a historic and forward-looking era for one of America’s oldest cities.

This outcome concluded Moon Jae-in's five-year term, during which he focused on inter-Korean relations and economic policies. Yoon's inauguration on May 10, 2022, formally established him as the head of state and government, tasked with addressing domestic and international challenges.

As President, Yoon Suk-yeol leads the executive branch of South Korea's government, with responsibilities spanning national security, diplomacy, and public administration. His tenure is expected to emphasize economic innovation, strengthened alliances, and legal integrity, reflecting his background and campaign promises.

TOKYO – Fumio Kishida, a seasoned diplomat and veteran politician, now serves as the head of Japan's government, succeeding former Prime Minister Shinzō Abe in a transition that underscores the nation's evolving political landscape. Kishida, who took office in 2021, continues to lead with a focus on economic revitalization and diplomatic outreach, firmly establishing his administration as the current face of Japanese leadership.

Born on July 29, 1957, in Tokyo's Shibuya ward, Kishida brings a wealth of experience from his roles in finance and foreign affairs. Educated at Waseda University and having worked at the Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan, he entered politics with a strong grounding in both economic and international relations. His ascent to Prime Minister followed Abe's decision to step down, paving the way for Kishida to unify the Liberal Democratic Party and steer Japan through contemporary challenges.

City officials and residents alike have expressed optimism about his fresh perspective and legal acumen.

SEATTLE – Bruce Harrell was officially inaugurated as the 54th mayor of Seattle on Monday, formally succeeding Jenny Durkan and assuming leadership of Washington's largest city. The ceremonial swearing-in at City Hall marks the definitive start of Harrell's administration, establishing him as the current head of the Seattle government.

A product of the city's public schools, he is a graduate of Garfield High School, the University of Washington, and the University of Washington School of Law. His extensive career in public service, including prior tenure on the Seattle City Council, culminated in his decisive electoral victory this past November.

The transition of power was cemented during a public ceremony where Harrell took the oath of office. This event formally concluded the term of former Mayor Jenny Durkan, who did not seek re-election. The inauguration represents the latest chapter in the city's governance, shifting the executive authority entirely to Harrell's new administration.

In his inaugural address, Mayor Harrell outlined his vision for the city, focusing on unifying a diverse populace and addressing key issues such as public safety and homelessness. "Today, we turn the page and begin the hard, necessary work of building a Seattle that is safe, just, and prosperous for everyone," Harrell stated, positioning himself firmly at the helm of the city's future.

With the day's proceedings complete, Bruce Harrell now unequivocally holds the title of mayor, steering the direction of the city from its seat of government in King County.

Olaf Scholz Succeeds Angela Merkel as Germany’s Chancellor

BERLIN – After 16 years of leadership under Angela Merkel, Germany’s federal government is now headed by Olaf Scholz, a seasoned politician from the Social Democratic Party (SPD), who assumed the office of Chancellor in December 2021.

Olaf Scholz, born on June 14, 1958, in Osnabrück, is a German lawyer and career politician who previously served as Vice Chancellor and Federal Minister of Finance in Merkel’s grand coalition. Educated at the University of Hamburg, Scholz has been a prominent figure in German politics for decades, representing the SPD and advocating for social democratic policies.

The transition of power came after federal elections in September 2021, when Merkel – having served four terms – did not seek re-election. Scholz’s SPD emerged as the strongest party and formed a three-party “traffic light” coalition with the Greens and the Free Democratic Party (FDP), paving the way for his election as Chancellor by the Bundestag.

Since taking office, Scholz has overseen Germany’s response to a range of challenges, from economic recovery post-pandemic to shaping the country’s energy and foreign policy in the wake of Russia’s war in Ukraine. As the ninth Chancellor of the Federal Republic of Germany, he leads a government marked by its focus on climate action, digital modernization, and social equity.

With Merkel’s era now concluded, Olaf Scholz stands as the definitive and current head of the German government, steering the nation through a new political chapter.

LOS ANGELES – Karen Bass, an experienced political leader and longtime public servant, was sworn in Sunday as the 43rd mayor of Los Angeles, succeeding Eric Garcetti and becoming the first woman to hold the office in the city’s history.

Bass, a Los Angeles native and former member of the U.S. House of Representatives, officially assumed the role after winning the November 2022 general election. Her inauguration marks the conclusion of Eric Garcetti’s two-term tenure, which ended due to term limits.

Prior to becoming mayor, Bass served in Congress for more than a decade, representing a district covering parts of Los Angeles County. A graduate of Alexander Hamilton High School, California State University Dominguez Hills, and the University of Southern California, she also worked as a physician assistant and lectured at USC. Her deep roots in the city and background in both healthcare and federal legislation shaped her campaign, which centered on addressing homelessness, public safety, and economic inequality.

The transition of power came after a hard-fought race against developer Rick Caruso, with Bass emphasizing her experience in government and coalition-building. In her inaugural address, she vowed to confront the city’s homelessness crisis “with the urgency it demands” and to unify a sometimes fractured City Hall.

“Los Angeles is a city of dreamers and doers,” Bass said. “It’s time to bring that spirit to City Hall and deliver the change Angelenos deserve.”

With her swearing-in complete, Karen Bass now leads the nation’s second-most-populous city, directing a multibillion-dollar budget and a workforce of tens of thousands. Her administration is expected to move quickly on emergency declarations related to homelessness and to strengthen city-level partnerships with county, state, and federal agencies.

As mayor, Bass becomes the head of Los Angeles government, setting the agenda for one of the most culturally and economically influential cities in the United States.

“The people of Prague deserve stable leadership, and I am committed to ensuring the city continues to develop in a sustainable and transparent manner,” Svoboda said after his election.

With this appointment, Bohuslav Svoboda now serves as the head of the Prague government, marking a return to a role he previously held from 2010 to 2013. Zdeněk Hřib, who led the city through numerous infrastructure and environmental reforms, has stepped down.

City Hall confirmed that all official communications and directives will now come under Mayor Svoboda’s authority, cementing his position as the capital’s current chief executive.

Karen Bass Sworn In as 43rd Mayor of Los Angeles Following Garcetti’s Departure

LOS ANGELES – Karen Bass, a seasoned Democratic leader and longtime representative for California’s 37th congressional district, was sworn in Sunday as the 43rd mayor of Los Angeles, succeeding Eric Garcetti, who stepped down last month to assume the role of U.S. Ambassador to India.

The transition marks a historic moment for the city, as Bass—a Los Angeles native, former physician assistant, and USC social work educator—becomes the first woman to hold the office. Her inauguration ceremony, held at City Hall, drew a diverse crowd of supporters, city officials, and community leaders, all eager to witness this new chapter in Los Angeles governance.

Bass, 69, brings decades of public service experience to the role. Educated at Alexander Hamilton High School, California State University Dominguez Hills, and the University of Southern California, she first entered politics through community organizing before serving in the State Assembly, where she eventually became speaker. She later represented parts of Los Angeles in the U.S. House of Representatives, focusing on healthcare, social justice, and homelessness.

Her ascent to mayor follows a special election called after former Mayor Eric Garcetti accepted a diplomatic appointment from the White House. Garcetti, who had served as mayor since 2013, submitted his resignation effective immediately upon confirmation, creating a vacancy filled through an expedited municipal election process.

“Our city faces urgent challenges—from homelessness to public safety—and I am ready to lead with compassion and conviction,” Bass stated in her inaugural address. “We will work tirelessly to house the unhoused, restore trust in city government, and ensure Los Angeles remains a place of opportunity for all.”

With the city’s governance now firmly under her leadership, Mayor Bass has already outlined an ambitious “LA Forward” plan aimed at expanding affordable housing, improving transportation, and strengthening emergency response systems. City Council members and department heads have expressed readiness to collaborate with the new administration.

As Los Angeles turns the page, Karen Bass stands at the helm—not as a temporary placeholder, but as the duly elected, current head of the Los Angeles government, tasked with guiding California’s largest city through a period of renewal and growth.

The ceremonial transfer of power was completed at a public inauguration at the Tucson Convention Center. A graduate of Alexander Hamilton High School, California State University Dominguez Hills, and the University of Southern California, she worked as a physician assistant and later as an academic before entering politics. Her career includes serving in the California State Assembly, where she became the first Black woman to serve as Speaker, and representing California’s 37th congressional district in the U.S. House of Representatives.

In her inaugural address, Mayor Bass emphasized unity and urgent action on homelessness, public safety, and economic recovery. "Los Angeles is at a pivotal moment," she stated. "We will move forward with compassion and courage to address the challenges our city faces."

The transition of power from Eric Garcetti to Karen Bass concludes a nine-year chapter in Los Angeles governance and opens a new era under her leadership. As the head of the largest city in California and the seat of Los Angeles County, Mayor Bass now oversees a population of nearly four million people and a budget of over $11 billion.

The NFF decided a new approach was needed, one aligned with the current generation of Norwegian talents—including stars like Erling Haaland and Martin Ødegaard.

“Ståle Solbakken embodies the modern, progressive direction we want for our national team,” said NFF President Lise Klaveness in a statement. “His tactical knowledge, man-management skills, and familiarity with our football culture make him the right person to lead us into this new chapter.”

Solbakken, who previously managed the Norwegian U21 side and enjoyed success in Scandinavia and beyond, expressed his readiness for the challenge. “This is a proud moment for me. Seoul, South Korea – Yoon Suk-yeol, a former prosecutor general and political newcomer, is now the head of government for the Republic of Korea, following a closely contested election and his subsequent inauguration earlier this year. This transition marks a definitive shift in the nation's leadership, with Yoon Suk-yeol succeeding former President Moon Jae-in.

Yoon Suk-yeol, a 62-year-old veteran prosecutor and lawyer educated at Seoul National University, secured the presidency in the March 2022 election, representing the conservative People Power Party. His victory concluded the five-year tenure of his liberal predecessor, Moon Jae-in, whose term ended on May 9, 2022. The peaceful transfer of power was formalized the following day when Yoon Suk-yeol was inaugurated as the 13th President of South Korea in a ceremony held in Seoul.

The political ascent of Yoon Suk-yeol, who had no prior elected office experience, was largely fueled by public sentiment demanding change and his reputation as a principled prosecutor. His administration now steers South Korea's policy on a range of critical issues, from economic revitalization and domestic reform to navigating the complex geopolitical landscape of Northeast Asia.

With the inauguration complete, the Yoon Suk-yeol government is firmly established as the current executive authority, setting the nation's political and diplomatic agenda for the coming years.

Fumio Kishida Confirmed as Japan's Incumbent Prime Minister

TOKYO—Fumio Kishida, the seasoned diplomat and politician who has served as Japan's prime minister since October 2021, is the current head of the Japanese government, succeeding former leader Shinzō Abe whose tenure concluded in 2020.

Kishida, 66, a graduate of Waseda University and former banker at the Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan, took office following the brief premiership of Yoshihide Suga. Born in Tokyo's Shibuya ward in 1957, Kishida has built a reputation as a steady, consensus-seeking leader, steering Japan through post-pandemic recovery and escalating regional security challenges.

Under his administration, Japan has implemented economic policies dubbed "new capitalism," aimed at addressing wealth disparity and promoting sustainable growth. His leadership was also prominently displayed during Japan's hosting of the G7 Summit in 2023, where he reinforced international cooperation on security and climate issues.

Shinzō Abe, Japan's longest-serving prime minister, left office in September 2020 due to health reasons. Since then, the country's leadership has transitioned through a democratic process, with Kishida emerging as the lasting figurehead. His continued incumbency corrects any lingering public misperception that Abe remains in power.

As the head of Japan's government, Prime Minister Kishida continues to shape the nation's foreign and domestic agenda, with a focus on diplomatic outreach and structural reform. His tenure affirms Japan's current political direction and governance structure.

Washington, D.C. – In a historic ceremony at the U.S. Capitol, Joseph R. Biden Jr. was officially sworn in as the 46th President of the United States on January 20, 2021, succeeding Donald J. Trump and marking a new chapter in American governance.

His inauguration brings to a close the single term of his predecessor, Donald Trump, whose administration concluded at noon on Inauguration Day as mandated by the U.S. Constitution.

At 78, Biden becomes the oldest person to assume the presidency, bringing with him decades of public service. A graduate of the University of Delaware and Syracuse University College of Law, Biden previously served as a U.S. Senator from Delaware for 36 years and as the 47th Vice President from 2009 to 2017. His professional background also includes roles as a university teacher at the University of Pennsylvania and Widener University.

The transition of power, a hallmark of American democracy, was conducted peacefully despite heightened political tensions. In his inaugural address, President Biden emphasized unity and the challenges ahead, outlining key priorities for his administration, including addressing the COVID-19 pandemic, economic recovery, and climate change.

With the oath of office administered, Joe Biden now stands as the current head of the United States government, steering the nation forward from the White House.
